description: JSON-driven queries for Entity Framework Core. A powerful, versatile library for dynamically composing complex filter, sort, paginate, group, aggregate, and set-operation (Union / Intersect / Except) expressions — all driven by simple JSON objects from any front-end or API consumer. Three composable shapes (Filter / Segment / Summary), twenty-eight extension methods, nested navigation through references and collections with auto-wrapped .Any() lambdas, heterogeneous Condition.Values with type-safe coercion, and a thread-safe reflection cache with five tuned presets (FIFO / LRU / LFU). Since 3.0 it also carries an opt-in field-level policy layer: attributes and runtime rules decide what each caller may filter, sort, select, group, aggregate and see, with masking, tokenization, forced predicates and a k-anonymity floor. On PostgreSQL the case-insensitive pattern operators can opt in to ILIKE, so a trigram index serves them. Targets .NET 6+. Free Forever. Full reference, JSON cookbook, and tuning guide at https://doc.dynamicwhere.com.
releaseNotes:
v3.5.0 — A row type can refuse a caller's projection inside the policy gate, where the refusal is traced and audited; the case-insensitive pattern operators can match by ILIKE on PostgreSQL, so a trigram index serves them; a type's default order can end a caller's orders as a tiebreak, so paging is total; and a summary with no grouping is refused as a malformed request rather than failing as a server error.

New: [DwEntity(RefuseSelects = true)] refuses a non-empty Selects for a type meant to be read whole, such as a read-only projection, where a partial row would report defaults for every member the caller did not name. It throws PolicyException with the new PolicyErrorCode.SelectsRefused (23), and since the refusal is the gate's own it is traced, audited when AuditRefusals is on, and reported by the simulator, which a host refusing the list in its endpoint could never do. The names are gated first: under the strict tier a name the caller may not select, or one that matches nothing, is still refused as FieldDeniedForSelect and audited under its own path; a list whose every name was dropped is still AllSelectsDenied; only a list of selectable names reaches SelectsRefused. Both tiers refuse, and a dry run records the decision and runs as written. It covers the Filter terminals, ToListAsync with a Segment, the composable Filter, FilterDynamic, Select and SelectDynamic, and the simulator; a null or empty Selects and the projection the policy synthesizes to withhold denied fields are never refused. PolicySchema.RefusesSelects says so once for the entity, leaving CanSelect to mean what it meant, and PolicyModelValidator warns when the flag stands without RequirePolicy, because an unguarded query never reads it. A [DwEntity] on a derived type replaces the base type's, as for RequirePolicy and DefaultOrder.

New: DwText.Configure(o => o.CaseInsensitive = TextMatching.ILike), or "DynamicWhere": { "Text": { "CaseInsensitive": "ILike" } } through DwTextOptions.Bind, compiles IContains, INotContains, IStartsWith, INotStartsWith, IEndsWith and INotEndsWith to column ILIKE pattern ESCAPE '\' through Npgsql's EF.Functions.ILike, which a pg_trgm GIN or GiST index on the column can serve where lower(column) LIKE cannot. Percent, underscore and the escape character in a value are escaped, so it still matches as text; against PostgreSQL 16 it returns the same rows as lowering for every pattern operator. Opt-in and process-wide, with the default unchanged: only a query EF Core's own provider translates is rewritten, so LINQ to objects and a wrapping provider keep lowering, but every EF Core query in the process is, so a process that also queries another database through EF Core must not choose it. IEqual, INotEqual, IIn and INotIn stay lower(column) = value, which an index on lower(column) serves, and HAVING stays lowered. Npgsql.EntityFrameworkCore.PostgreSQL is found by name when the options are configured, so a deployment without it refuses to start; an identical second Configure does nothing and a different one is refused.

New: [DwEntity(DefaultOrderAsTiebreak = true)], or DwPolicyOptions.DefaultOrderAsTiebreak for every type that declares a DefaultOrder, ends a guarded caller's orders with every default field the caller did not name, after the caller's last Sort and in its declared direction, so rows tied on the caller's fields keep one order from page to page instead of one row showing on two pages and another on none. A field the caller names keeps the caller's place and direction, and a field this caller may not order by is left out, as the default always left it out. It covers the Filter terminals, ToListAsync with a Segment, the composable Filter, FilterDynamic and Order, and the simulator; a projection that could hide a default field, one composed on the handle, and a Summary never take it. The order is total only when the default ends with a unique field such as the key. Off by default; the option freezes with the posture, binds from DefaultOrderAsTiebreak and is compared by a second Configure, and PolicyModelValidator warns when the attribute is set on a type with no usable DefaultOrder.

Behaviour change: a Summary whose GroupBy is null is refused with LogicException GroupByMustHasAtLeastOneField, as an empty grouping always was, by every summary terminal, guarded or not, before anything reads the request. It escaped as ArgumentNullException, which a host answers as a server error. PolicySimulator.Simulate with such a summary now throws the same LogicException rather than reporting a query that would run.

v3.4.0 — Page caps per declared purpose, so an export reads every match in one statement while a search keeps its page; security fixes for struct members, a transform on one now applied, a member of a nullable struct now policed and a typed selection beneath a list of structs no longer handing back a denied member; a path through a member a constructor builds is refused rather than run; the parts of a struct take the struct member's policy; and a typed selection through a struct returns its values.

v3.3.0 — A second host may configure the same posture, a path no database can compute is refused rather than run, a path or a member the attribute walk cannot name is still policed, a malformed request is refused as one rather than reaching the caller as a server error, a token vault can hold a key, and Clone is public on the three request types.

v3.2.0 — A row projected before ApplyPolicy keeps its nested objects and lists, denials the policy gate could not see are enforced, a declared default order reaches projected rows, and every asynchronous terminal takes a CancellationToken.

v3.1.0 — Date comparisons that work on every date member, segments combined in the database, five new caps, a stable code where a sentence used to be, preparation enforced whether or not a store is configured, a policy bypass through members named Root, It or Parent closed, a long In list that ended the process fixed, the names the expression parser keeps refused by name, a strict tier that no longer discloses its trace or which fields exist, forced predicates that can let rows with no value through, a declared default order for guarded queries, and refused queries written to the audit.

v3.0.0 — Field-level policies. A new layer that decides what each caller may filter, sort, select, group, aggregate, and see. Additive: nothing enforces until you opt in, and a project with no policy attributes and no DwPolicy.Configure call behaves exactly as 2.1.5.

v2.1.5 — Documentation only. Fixes the XML documentation shipped with the package, which drives IntelliSense in consuming projects: an unescaped generic argument in the Select<T> comment truncated its remarks and returns text, three ToList/ToListAsync overloads were missing the getQueryString parameter description, and CacheReporting.GetQuickHealthSummary documented a parameter it does not take. The library now builds with zero warnings. No API or behaviour changes from 2.1.4.

v2.1.4 — Security and correctness fix. Recommended for all users.

v2.1.3 — Licensing: now published under the MIT license (SPDX: MIT). Free forever for commercial and personal use, with no license acceptance required. No API or behaviour changes from 2.1.2.

v2.1.2 — Fix: ordering by a field path that crosses a collection navigation (e.g. "Tags.Value" on List<Tag>) threw "No property or field 'Value' exists in type 'List`1'". Collection segments are now aggregated to a single comparable value — Min ascending, Max descending — at any nesting depth, translated to SQL and safe over empty collections in memory.
